title: the qc arm of pattern_extract_titles anchors on the **Finding**: label, but the authoritative QC finding-line format (agents/edm-qc-auditor.md:59-63, restated verbatim at skills/implement/SKILL.md:122-126, which owns the qc-summary.md merge) carries no such label -- a conforming qc-summary.md extracts zero titles and the arm records no-recognized-findings permanently

pattern_extract_titles hand-rolls fence detection in three copies with a ^-anchored ``` pattern, so an indented fence never toggles infence and a quoted example '### CA-NNN' heading is harvested as a real pattern -- while the function's own comment at :5197-5198 claims parity with pattern_insert_line_for, which resolves fences through _edm-lint-lib.sh's classifier whose documented contract explicitly covers indented fences

the code arm's post-ID delimiter class [ \t:(] excludes / and -, so the plugin's own dominant compound-ID heading form (G21/CA-233, G16/CA-355, G13/CA-391) is not recognised as a finding; a mixed report still reports extraction_status=ok with a silently short count, which is the one state documented to mean 'clean round'

lint:hooks-shell's jq extraction selects on .type=="command" without requiring a non-empty string .command, so an entry with the key absent writes the literal text 'null' to the temp file; bash -n and shellcheck --shell=sh both accept it and the blocking gate over the plugin's most privileged shell prints OK for a hook it never checked
